market.worldSizeUSD_B_range: India aerospace parts manufacturing market: $13.6B (2023) to $21.48B by 2030 (6.8%/yr). A separately-scoped global 'aerospace parts manufacturing market' figure ($971.99M to $1,381.84M by 2032) is far smaller than India's own standalone figure and appears to use a narrower definition — not treated as comparable.
exportGeographies: primarily intra-group to France (parent-group structures common in this segment) and other prime-OEM destinations — see company-specific notes
globalCompetitors: not applicable at India-segment scale — this segment is largely Tier-1/Tier-2 supply into global OEMs (Boeing, Airbus, Safran, GE, Rolls-Royce) rather than a competitive market with rival 'products'
market.domesticSlice: Asia-Pacific aerospace parts manufacturing specifically is forecast to grow fastest, 17.3%/yr (2025-2032). India defense manufacturing indigenization is expected to rise from under 40% to potentially 70%+ over the coming decade; defense exports grew from ₹6.8B (FY14) to ₹236B (FY25); Defence Industrial Corridors set up in Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu

structureFacts: GST 2.0 reforms cut/abolished GST on defense equipment and drones to boost indigenization

NADCAP accreditation lets OEMs/Tier-1s fast-track supplier audits — a company must be AS9100-certified before NADCAP auditing occurs, and NADCAP approval is often required for specific critical manufacturing processes by OEM customers

adoptionStructure.note: Long-term, multi-year supply agreements typical of aerospace tier-1/tier-2 relationships — orders are platform-life-length rather than transactional, reflecting the qualification burden and switching costs inherent to AS9100/NADCAP-gated aerospace supply chains

peers.name: Azad Engineering
peers.note: the closest true segment comparable — precision-forged/machined aerospace & energy components; new contracts with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Baker Hughes; customers incl. GE, Honeywell, Rolls-Royce, Safran, Siemens

peers.name: Data Patterns (India)
peers.note: defense electronics/systems (radars, EW), not precision-machined components — an adjacent-sector benchmark, not a direct peer
